title: Congress creates the program
body: Section 3025 of the Affordable Care Act adds the Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program to the Social Security Act, section 1886(q).

title: Penalties begin, capped at 1%
body: Three conditions count: heart attack, heart failure, and pneumonia.

title: Cap rises to 2%
body: The statute steps the maximum reduction up each year until it reaches 3%.

title: Cap reaches 3%; COPD and hip/knee replacement added
body: The 3% maximum is set in law and has not changed since.

title: Bypass surgery added; pneumonia definition widened
body: The pneumonia group now includes aspiration pneumonia and sepsis with pneumonia present on admission.

title: Congress orders peer comparisons
body: The 21st Century Cures Act requires CMS to compare each hospital with hospitals serving similar shares of patients who have both Medicare and full Medicaid.

title: Peer grouping starts
body: Hospitals are sorted into five peer groups by dual-eligible share and judged against their group's median. A neutrality modifier keeps total penalties the same as the old method.

title: COVID-19: early-2020 data set aside
body: CMS excludes claims from January through June 2020. The gap shows up in the FY2022 through FY2024 calculations.

title: Pneumonia sits out a year
body: CMS suppresses the pneumonia measure for FY2023 and removes COVID-19 patients from the other measures.

title: Pneumonia returns
body: Patients with a COVID-19 diagnosis stay out of every measure through FY2026.

title: Medicare Advantage patients counted; two-year window
body: Adopted in the FY2026 rule: readmission ratios now include Medicare Advantage patients, the data window shrinks from three years to two, and the COVID-19 exclusion ends. The cut still applies only to traditional Medicare payments.

title: Next: sepsis
body: The FY2027 rule adds a seventh measure, readmission after sepsis. Hospitals get confidential reports for FY2028 and FY2029; it counts toward penalties starting FY2030.
